text:
Marta: quick heads-up — canary run on the new kernel selection + batch heuristic showed bad memory patterns
Alex: which nodes? logs?
Marta: 4 x A100-80GB, single model variant (gptx-small-q4). Repro: steady 200 rps with mixed short/long requests. Observed frequent OOMy recycler churn + KV prefill spikes.
Marta: perf dump:
```
run: canary-2026-03-16
requests: 2000
oom_count: 9
kv_occupancy: 0.78
kv_frag: 0.23
avg_token_latency_ms: baseline 12 -> canary 21
prefill_rate: 0.45
decode_kv_use: 0.65
```
Devon: ouch. kv_frag 23% is high. what's allocator config?
Marta: using slab-sizes [1MB,4MB,16MB], recycle_threshold=0.6, prefill_soft_cap=60MB/request
Priya: prefill_soft_cap 60MB/request is aggressive for mixed seqs. Try per-request cap of 24MB and a trim-pass after heavy prefill.
Alex: also noticed kernel change (fused-attn v2) increased workspace peak by ~14% in worst-case. helps latency under small batches but blows up with mixed long tails.
Kai: hypothesis: prefill => alloc many small slabs => fragmentation => recycler can't coalesce => OOM under burst. Proposed mitigations:
- lower per-request prefill cap
- add compact-after-prefill trim pass (non-blocking)
- opportunistic buffer reuse across requests ("mem-sculptor")
- prefer fused kernel only when seq_len < 512
Marta: ran quick bench with per-req cap=24MB + trim-pass every 100ms, results:
```
oom_count: 1 / 2000
kv_frag: 0.12
avg_token_latency_ms: 14
cost_tokens: -8%
```
Devon: nice. can we simulate at scale? need a mem-reclaim microbench in perf-suite (repro script + artifact).
Alex: I'll add a canary that toggles fused kernel based on seq histogram and apply per-req cap. Also instrument KV slab allocation tags (caller, seq_len, alloc_size).
Priya: I'll prototype trim-pass: incremental free-list coalesce with cap on work-per-ms so no global GC pauses.
sre-bot: Incident created #INC-2026-347 for canary OOMs, assigned to eng-runtime.
Marta: thanks. @Alex @Priya @Devon can we get an action list by EOD? I'll attach perf traces + repro to the ticket.
Alex: yep. starting now. :thumbsup:
Devon: reusing buffer pools will need careful lifetime tracking, but big win. drafting design doc.
Kai: one more note — avoid global GC pauses: make trim-pass incremental and bound latency cost (work budget tied to idle cycles).
Marta: leaving notes in the ticket with stack traces and the small repro script, putting raw dumps in /mnt/perf/canary-2026-03-16. thanks all."
